items.title: Unfazed Hughes burns former team as Wild hand Canucks another loss
items.summary: Favour was few and far between for Quinn Hughes in his return to Vancouver. But on the scoreboard, it was Hughes who got the last laugh against his former team.
items.body: VANCOUVER — Quinn Hughes had listened to about 33 minutes of near-constant boos and jeers. He heard an energized crowd at Rogers Arena break out into various chants: Quinn, you suck; He’s not signing; Quit-ter. He watched as the jumbotron highlighted several disgruntled fans in retrofitted Hughes jerseys, letting the former captain know exactly where he stands with the Vancouver Canucks faithful after his departure last December. By the 34th minute of that, Hughes decided, presumably, that he had enough. Unfazed by the hostility around him, the Minnesota Wild defenceman calmly corralled a rebound in front of goaltender Leevi Merilainen, potting potentially the easiest and most memorable goal of his career — and his 500th career point — and dealing the death blow to the Canucks. Hughes got the Brady Tkachuk treatment. Unlike Tkachuk, it was Hughes who got the last laugh against his former team. “I wasn’t thinking about it like that. I just wanted to get a win,” Hughes said post-game about scoring his milestone goal where it all got started. “I think just seeing those fans and being able to play here again is just pretty cool for me.” It helps, of course, that his team got the win and Hughes finished with the game-winning goal, an assist and first-star honours — no wonder it was easy to let the boos roll off his back. There was some acclaim scattered amongst the antagonists. His tribute during the first TV timeout was met with a mixed bag of reactions: some leers, some cheers and a fair few standing ovations. But outside of the minute-long homage, favour for the 27-year-old was few and far between. “Very passionate fanbase,” Hughes said. “I was here for six and a half years, tried my best, and to see, you know, (I) got some cheers there. items.summary: WINNIPEG -- Jacob Fowler didn’t want the night to end even though the Montreal Canadiens were clinging to a one-goal lead as time was winding down at the 2026 Tim Hortons Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium here Sunday.
items.body: Montreal’s 21-year-old wins fifth straight start, making 33 saves WINNIPEG -- Jacob Fowler didn’t want the night to end even though the Montreal Canadiens were clinging to a one-goal lead as time was winding down at the 2026 Tim Hortons Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium here Sunday. The Montreal Canadiens goalie soaked up as much of the atmosphere as he could in the 2-1 win against the Winnipeg Jets, becoming the youngest goalie to play and win an NHL outdoor game. “This game was different than a lot of other games I played where a lot of times, you’re looking at the clock kind of waiting for it to run out,” Fowler said. “Obviously you want to get the win, but I think tonight was one of those games where you never want the game to end. “It’s so fun to be out there. The two of us (defenseman Lane Hutson ) we’ve been talking about it. We wish we can play more of these. It’s so fun, it’s such a great environment, the ice was pretty good, so it’s just a lot of fun, I definitely took in my fair share of the moment there.” Fowler made 33 saves in the win, earning first star honors. At 21 years and 355 days, he was the youngest goalie in the history of the NHL to start an outdoor game. The win was his fifth straight, improving his record to 5-1-0 this season in six games (all starts) with a 1.79 goals-against average and a .924 save percentage. “He’s dialed in, in there,” Canadiens defenseman Noah Dobson said. “I feel when goalies are at the top of their game, they obviously make it look easy, even though it’s not easy at all; some of those seam plays, post to post, it’s tough. items.body: VANCOUVER — Quinn Hughes notched the 500th point of his NHL career in his return to Vancouver, and his Minnesota Wild doubled up the Canucks 4-2 on Sunday. Boos rained down on Hughes virtually every time he touched the puck, but the former Canucks captain received a partial standing ovation and audible cheers during a video tribute early in the first period. Hughes, Kirill Kaprizov and Maxim Shabanov each had a goal and an assist for the Wild (8-3-2), who were coming off a 5-1 victory over the Kraken in Seattle on Saturday. Bobby Brink also found the back of the net for his first tally of the season and Calvin Pickard stopped 16 of the 18 shots he faced for Minnesota. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser both found the back of the net for the Canucks (2-10-1) in the third period. Leevi Merilainen made 30 saves for Vancouver, which lost its 10th straight game. The team has not won since Oct. 3, when it beat the Calgary Flames 4-1. The Wild opened the scoring late in the first on Sunday after Filip Chytil was called for high-sticking. Kaprizov sliced a pass across the top of the crease to Shabanov, who tapped a shot in backdoor with 87 seconds left in the frame. Brink doubled the lead at the 5:54 mark of the second after Chytil turned the puck over along the boards. Michael McCarron picked it up and snapped it to Brink, who drove in, pulling Merilainen out of his crease, then wrapped a shot around the goalie to make it 2-0. With Minnesota on another power play midway through the second, Hughes swiped a rebound in backdoor to boost the Wild's lead. items.summary: Jacob Fowler looked cool and composed, like he always does; like a kid just yucking it up with his buddies on a backyard rink rather than one playing under the nation’s watch. The Canadiens goalie was the best player on the ice in the Heritage Classic.
items.body: WINNIPEG — Leave it to the kid from Florida to steal the show in Winnipeg. That’s what Jacob Fowler did Sunday at Princess Auto Stadium, earning the Montreal Canadiens a 2-1 win over the Winnipeg Jets in the Heritage Classic, and showing just how prepared he is to step up under the spotlight. This was the 21-year-old’s biggest game of the 23 he’s played in this league to date. The native of Melbourne, Fla. came into it as the youngest goaltender to ever start an NHL outdoor game, though you’d never know it watching him thwart all but one Jets chance in a 33-save performance. Fowler looked like a seasoned veteran all the way through. He looked cool and composed, like he always does; like a kid just yucking it up with his buddies on a backyard rink rather than one playing under the nation’s watch — in the centre of a massive field surrounded by 32,343 fans in one of hockey’s most unique atmospheres. When you think about what that means about Fowler, you know it bodes extremely well for both him and the Canadiens. They’re a team rising towards perennial contention, and he’s a star in the making at the most important position. “It’s a ton of pressure being a starting goalie, and it’s a ton of pressure being the starting goalie on the Canadiens,” said Jake Evans. “I think he kind of just pushes that aside and believes in himself and he doesn’t really worry about all the outside noise.” It’s been deafening ever since amateur scout Billy Ryan pounded the table at a 2023 pre-draft meeting for the Canadiens to take Fowler. items.body: Defenseman also discusses being named captain, facing Ovechkin with NHL.com Welcome to the NHL Chat Room, NHL.com's weekly Q&A feature where we talk to key figures in the game, gaining insight into their lives on and off the ice. This week, we feature Los Angeles Kings defenseman Drew Doughty. WASHINGTON -- As Drew Doughty approaches his 37th birthday on Dec. 8, the Los Angeles Kings defenseman naturally has reasons to contemplate how much longer he wants to continue playing. Doughty has seen longtime teammates and peers retire and this, his 19th NHL season, is the final season of his eight-year, $88 million contract. But he believes he has a few more seasons left in him. “I think I can play until over 40,” Doughty said last week. “I believe I can. I’ve just got to stay healthy. The want to do it hasn't dropped, so, until I lose that, I'm not going to retire.” Like former teammates Dustin Brown (18 seasons) and Anze Kopitar (20 seasons), Doughty hopes to play his entire career with Los Angeles, the team that selected him with the No. 2 pick in the 2008 NHL Draft and with which he won the Stanley Cup in 2012 and 2014 and the Norris Trophy as the League’s top defenseman in 2016. And Kings general manager Ken Holland said during the offseason that he intends to re-sign Doughty before he can become an unrestricted free agent on July 1, 2027. Although contract talks with Holland have yet to advance beyond the preliminary stage, Doughty made it clear he’s willing to do whatever it takes to remain with Los Angeles. “He knows what I want. I believe he wants me to stay,” Doughty said. “We just haven't talked about it yet. I feel like I'm performing better than I have in my past two seasons. items.body: VANCOUVER — A chorus of boos echoed through Rogers Arena as Quinn Hughes stepped on the ice for warm-ups on Sunday. The former Vancouver Canucks captain was back inside the rink for the first time since being traded to the Minnesota Wild in December, and some fans vocally displayed their displeasure with the move. Hundreds of people — many clad in Canucks jerseys emblazoned with Hughes' name and No. 43 — stood around the glass ahead of warm-ups, hoping to get a glimpse of the star defenceman. One held a sign reading "And I thought I had commitment issues." Hughes came into Sunday's game knowing a frosty reception was possible. "I don’t know what to expect too much (on Sunday) but we’ll face that when it comes," he said Saturday. "Whether I’m booed or whatnot, it won’t change how I feel about that place and how grateful I am for the experiences I had there.” Chants of "Quinn you suck!" erupted in the first minute of the game. Moments later, they were followed by jeers of "Quit-er! Quit-er!" Fans booed once again as a tribute to the blue liner began on the big screen during the first TV timeout, transformed into a mixed review, with whistles and clapping, and some in the crowd standing in ovation. Hughes skated out from the bench and raised his stick in salute as both his current and former teammates tapped their sticks on the boards. The deal saw Vancouver acquire Marco Rossi and Liam Ohgren, defenceman Zeev Buium and the Wild's first-round pick in the 2026 NHL entry draft. items.title: ‘Quinn Hughes Sucks’ chants rain down as Canucks fans boo former team captain
items.summary: Hughes was captain of the Canucks before he was traded to the Wild in the middle of the 2025-26 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In a stretch of several star players returning to their previous home arenas, fans of the Vancouver Canucks had their opportunity to let their former captain Quinn Hughes know how they felt about him on Sunday night, and they did not miss it. It didn’t take long, with fans chanting “Quinn Hughes Sucks” right as the Minnesota Wild defender hit the ice for the first time. Fans also booed him during warmups, before also chanting “Quitter” later on. Hughes, now with the Wild after a trade last season, returned to Rogers Arena for the first time after a move that came about when he let Canucks brass know that he didn’t plan to sign an extension to his current contract. The American defender was greeted with a mix of cheers and boos during a video tribute that was shared about seven minutes into the game. Hughes was drafted by the Canucks with the No. 7 overall pick in the first round of the 2018 NHL Draft. Over the ensuing seven years, he became very arguably the best defenseman in the history of the franchise. items.body: DALLAS — Jason Robertson scored twice and the Dallas Stars had a three-goal third period in a 6-3 victory over the New York Islanders on Sunday night. Robertson’s breakaway at 9:45 of the third period came five minutes after Wyatt Johnston’s tiebreaker. Mikko Rantanen added a goal four minutes after Robertson with his team-high sixth goal of the season. Tyler Seguin and Justin Hryckowian also scored for the Stars, who have won five consecutive games. Jake Oettinger made 16 saves. Defenseman Matthew Schaefer, Kyle Palmieri and Brayden Schenn scored for the Islanders, who erased three one-goal deficits only to lose two straight (0-1-1) for the first time this season. Sunday marked the Dallas return of Pete DeBoer, who took over the Islanders with four games to play last season. DeBoer was fired by the Stars in June 2025 after losing in the conference finals in each of his three Dallas seasons. The Stars have 20 straight penalty kills through its last five games, three on Sunday. The game was Dallas’ third in a six-game homestand and began a three-game Central Division trip for New York. Hryckowian’s younger brother, Dylan, and fellow forward Matthew Seminoff made their NHL debuts on Dallas' fourth line. The brothers were in the starting lineup.

Reimer had signed a professional tryout agreement with the Rangers' AHL affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack, 10 days ago. A fourth-round pick in the 2006 NHL Draft, Reimer spent his first eight seasons in the pros with the Toronto Maple Leafs organization. He then played for the Florida Panthers, Carolina Hurricanes, San Jose Sharks, Detroit Red Wings, Anaheim Ducks and Buffalo Sabres before joining the Senators. Sunday’s Heritage Classic against the Winnipeg Jets (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. CT) will be Guhle’s first NHL open-air experience, and despite the uniqueness of playing under the bright lights, and in front of more than 30,000 fans expected at Princess Auto Stadium, it’ll be a callback to when he first fell in love with the game, to when it was about nothing more than fun with friends. Only this time, no extra layers will be required, with the forecast calling for clear skies and a temperature of 3 C at puck drop. “That’s perfect,” said Oliver Kapanen, who played outdoor hockey every day after school in Timra, Finland, but has also never experienced anything like what he’ll live through on Sunday. Chris Kreider already has done it several times, so you can excuse him for not being as enthusiastic about it. “It’s only enjoyable if you win,” said the 35-year-old, who has a 3-0 record in outdoor NHL games but was on the wrong side of one in college, in his hometown, at Fenway Park, where he was first in awe of stepping foot in the Boston Red Sox room and then ultimately miserable sitting there after a loss. “It’s a dog and pony show, and if you lose it’s even more of a letdown,” Kreider added. “Two points, important to win a hockey game.” Phil Danault would love nothing more than for his Canadiens to beat the Jets after he lost with them to the Ottawa Senators in the NHL 100 Classic in 2017 at TD Place. “I lost another 6-1 to Minnesota when I was in my second season with Chicago, too,” said Danau

items.summary: After Zach Werenski seemingly had a foot out the door in Columbus this summer, could the Blue Jackets’ slow start have trade talks pick up around the defenceman once again? Michael Amato dives into Werenski’s future and more in his Sunday Overreactions.
items.body: If the goal for the Columbus Blue Jackets this season was to quiet the noise from the summer, it isn’t going well. Head coach Rick Bowness was none too pleased during training camp with the conditioning of a couple of players. Then, he went off on his team after it gave up a touchdown to the Florida Panthers last week. Kirill Marchenko’s return on Tuesday was supposed to bring out the best in the Blue Jackets, but a 6-2 defeat was all they could muster. Even with Saturday night’s desperately needed win over the Vegas Golden Knights, the Blue Jackets still sit last in the Eastern Conference, having accumulated just eight points in nine games. Columbus's problems are deeper than the standings, though. Marchenko didn’t hide the fact that he wanted out, and for a moment, it felt like Zach Werenski had one foot out the door this summer, as well. General manager Don Waddell and Werenski smoothed things over, but it may only have been a temporary reprieve. The reigning Norris Trophy winner’s contract doesn’t expire until the summer of 2028. But as we know, teams like to have clarity on their best players' intentions much earlier than that. That means the clock is ticking on Werenski, who is eligible to sign an extension next summer. We saw what the Vancouver Canucks did with Quinn Hughes and the Ottawa Senators with Brady Tkachuk, when it became clear both had no interest in re-signing. You could argue the Blue Jackets may even be in a more urgent state than the Canucks and Senators. Werenski at least thought seriously enough about moving on in the summer that Waddell was exploring trade options, before the two ultimately released a statement that reaffirmed Werenski’s commitment to the team. Lakovic then fired a one-timer from almost no angle past Senators goaltender Jackson Parsons. The tally marked Lakovic’s second AHL goal and his first career game-winner as a pro. items.title: Flames pay tribute to 2004 team with workmanlike victory
items.summary: On a night recognizing the 2004 team that came one win away from winning the Stanley Cup, the Flames did their best impression of that lunch pail crew to secure their third win in a row.
items.body: CALGARY — Going from the worst team in the league to one of the hottest teams in hockey, the Calgary Flames have turned an 0-5 start into a streak that has seen them win four of five. A 4-1 win over Detroit Saturday was their third in a row, and a perfect way to pay tribute to the 2004 team that fell one game short of winning the Stanley Cup. After all, you might recall, the team that re-energized a franchise with one of the most unlikely runs in modern NHL lore had barely made the playoffs that year. And while no one is suggesting the playoffs are a remote possibility in Year 1 of what promises to be a lengthy rebuild, the current crop of Craig Conroy’s kids have suddenly tapped into a similar elixir to the one that led Darryl Sutter’s crew to springtime euphoria. Combining hard work with airtight structure and all-world goaltending, the Flames have rebounded from a humiliating start in which the team was outscored by 19. Their latest win, once again on the back of goaltender Devin Cooley , has them tied with just a few other teams at 4-1 over their last five. With green hard hats dotting the Saddledome on Saturday night, in recognition of the organization’s workmanlike approach to slaying three playoff dragons 22 years ago, the Flames did their best impression of the lunch pail crew that electrified the city and might even have saved the organization. Wearing throwback jerseys from that year, which featured a black flaming C, black pants, gloves and helmets, they delighted the C of Red and a national TV audience with an unexpected win. They even got a game-opening goal eerily reminiscent of the conference semifinal series clincher Martin Gelinas scored in Game 6 to oust a Red Wings team that featured six Hall of Famers. items.title: Oilers’ lack of depth proves costly in loss to Maple Leafs
items.summary: The Oilers’ top line is beyond good. But the rest of the team ghosted in a blowout loss to the Maple Leafs on Saturday.
items.body: The Edmonton Oilers are a one-line team with a defenceman who is fourth in the NHL in scoring. And they can’t blame injuries for that anymore. “We need more, for sure,” said head coach Mike Babcock, whose team lost just their second game this season — but in regal fashion. It was a 7-2 blowout aired coast to coast, under the glare of the Saturday night lights against the Toronto Maple Leafs. There are the one or two nights a year that a coach should be able to count on a passionate effort from all 20 players. Leafs head coach Jim Hiller got it from his side. But Babcock? “Jim Hiller had his group playing harder than I had my group. That’s on me,” said Babcock. “It's a shame,” said Edmonton winger Kasperi Kapanen, after a pointless, minus-2 night for the former Leaf. “It's Saturday night against these guys. items.title: Nikita Kucherov sets Lightning team scoring record
items.summary: Nikita Kucherov passed Steven Stamkos for the most points in Tampa Bay Lightning franchise history.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-USA TODAY Sports There’s a new all-time points leader in Tampa Bay Lightning franchise history. Forward Nikita Kucherov assisted on Brayden Point’s power-play goal in the first period against the Utah Mammoth , which gave the Lightning a 3-1 lead and Kucherov the 1,138th point of his career, one more than Steven Stamkos’ franchise record and handing the title to the Tampa Bay winger. Kucherov tied the franchise record Wednesday after he scored against the Vegas Golden Knights . In 13 NHL regular seasons, Kucherov has 405 goals and 733 assists for 1,138 points in 890 career games. During that span, he’s recorded six 100-point campaigns, four 40-goal seasons and five 80-assist campaigns. In 2023-24, Kucherov became the fifth player in NHL history to record 100 assists in a single season . That season, he recorded career highs across the board with 44 goals and 100 assists for 144 points. He’s led the league in both assists and points three times during his career (2018-19, 2023-24 and 2024-25). Kucherov also recorded his 1,000th career point in 2025-26. Kucherov also scored 54 goals and recorded 123 assists for 177 points in 159 career playoff games. He was a major factor in the Lightning’s back-to-back Stanley Cup championships in 2020 and 2021, and helped the club reach the Stanley Cup Final two more times in 2015 and 2022. The native of Maykop, Russia, has earned several individual awards through his career. He won the Art Ross Trophy three times, the Hart Trophy twice and the Ted Lindsay Award twice. Going into Saturday night, the Lightning were 7-3-0 through their first 10 games of 2026-27. Kucherov and Brandon Hagel were tied for the team lead in points with 13.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google Alex Ovechkin secured a pretty sweet payday after playing in the Washington Capitals’ 4-3 overtime victory over the Buffalo Sabres on Saturday night. The game was Ovechkin’s 10th of the 2026-27 season, triggering the $4.75 million performance bonus in the one-year contract he signed with the Capitals to return for his 22nd and final NHL season . With the 10-game mark hit, Ovechkin will earn $9 million this year: $1 million in base salary and $3.25 million in signing bonus making up the remainder. Despite earning the bonus, Ovechkin’s cap hit this season will remain $4.25 million. However, depending on how much cap space the Capitals have at season’s end, a portion of Ovechkin’s bonus, or all of it, will carry over and count against next year’s salary cap even though the legendary winger will no longer be on the club’s roster. According to PuckPedia , the Capitals currently have $2.31 million in cap space, mainly because Rasmus Sandin is on long-term injured reserve. They project the Caps will be $1.36 million over the cap at season’s end, meaning the full Ovechkin bonus will likely extend into next year’s available funds. Through 10 games this season, the 41-year-old Ovechkin has notched just four points (1g, 3a), the weakest start to a campaign in his career. He is also playing a much smaller role than in previous years, skating just 14:12 per game coming into Saturday’s contest and no longer remaining on the ice for the full two minutes of Washington’s power plays. Ovechkin officially announced on October 5 that this season will be his last in the NHL. items.summary: William Nylander had two goals, including the 300th of his career, as the Toronto Maple Leafs scorched the Edmonton Oilers 7-2 on Saturday.
items.body: EDMONTON — William Nylander had two goals, including the 300th of his career, as the Toronto Maple Leafs scorched the Edmonton Oilers 7-2 on Saturday. Jack Roslovic, Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored for the Maple Leafs (7-4-2) who have won four straight. Anthony Stolarz made 30 stops to earn the win in the Toronto net. Leon Draisaitl scored twice for the Oilers (8-2-1) who had a three-game winning streak halted. With his league-leading 12th goal, Draisaitl recorded his third consecutive two-goal game and extended his goal-scoring streak to six games, during which he has nine goals. Maple Leafs: Matthews and Kirill Marchenko both extended their season-opening road point streak to five games. Matthews now needs just one point to reach 800 in his career, which will make him the fastest player in franchise history to reach the milestone, in addition to the NHL’s third quickest American skater to hit the mark. Oilers: Connor McDavid had two assists to extend his season-starting points streak to 11 games — giving him an incredible 33 points in 11 games. McDavid entered the contest scoring at a staggering 3.10 points-per-game rate. Just 54 seconds after going up 2-0, Kirill Marchenko made a nice pass to hit Stecher in flight in the slot and he scored his second goal of the season in as many games. No team has had more success in Rogers Place in Edmonton than the Maple Leafs. Since the Oilers moved into their new arena, Toronto has gone 12-2-1. items.title: Hurricanes tried trading for forward to flip to Jets for Hellebuyck
items.body: The reigning Stanley Cup champions were trying to make a blockbuster. Sportnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Saturday Headlines that the Carolina Hurricanes made a big effort to trade for Connor Hellebuyck , and they were willing to get creative to make a deal happen. "They tried to reach out to other teams to figure out forwards that the Jets might have interest in, and they were going to trade for those players, and flip that player to the Jets to get Hellebuyck," Friedman said. A deal never came to fruition, as Hellebuyck was sent to the New Jersey Devils on Friday for prospect Alexander Command, goalie Nico Daws, forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad and a pair of draft picks. Friedman added that the Jets wanted "immediate forward help" in the return for their long-time goalie, and the Hurricanes weren't willing to include players like Seth Jarvis, Logan Stankoven or Jackson Blake in a trade. So the Hurricanes tried other avenues, but were beaten to the punch by the Devils. Losing out on the Hellebuyck sweepstakes means Carolina will continue to roll with their goalie tandem of Brandon Bussi and Pyotr Kochetkov. Each netminder has started six games this season, with Kochetkov outperforming Bussi in both goals-against average and save percentage. The Hurricanes entered Saturday's game against the St. Louis Blues first in the Metropolitan Division with an 8-2-2 record.

items.body: Register Login Dallas Stars Injury Updates By Brennan McClain | at October 24, 2026 8:01 pm The Dallas Stars made an expected change to their injured reserve earlier today. Dallas announced that they placed forward Oskar Back on the long-term injured reserve and defenseman Esa Lindell on the normal injured reserve. Given that they’ve opened two roster spots, Dallas will likely recall a player from AHL Texas. Independent correspondent Robert Tiffin reports that the Stars will be without Sam Steel tomorrow after he received a treatment injection today. Forwards Radek Faksa and David Perron are also question marks, so it would make sense for the Stars to recall a forward. Back has been out of Dallas’ lineup since October 14th. The 26-year-old forward broke his finger in the Stars’ shootout win over the Colorado Avalanche, and isn’t expected back until mid-to-late November. With all due respect to Back, he should be fairly replaceable in Dallas’ bottom six. He scored nine goals and 28 points in 145 games throughout his first two years with the Stars, and has registered one assist in seven games this year. Meanwhile, Lindell will be much trickier to replace. Arguably the Stars’ top defensive defenseman, Lindell has been recovering from a lower-body injury since October 17th. Although he is eligible to return tomorrow, today’s roster move suggests he is not quite ready yet. However, Dallas will have the option to activate him when he is healthy in the coming days. On the year, Lindell has done what he does best. He’s gone scoreless in eight games, but has 18 blocked shots and has managed an exceptional 98.1% on-ice SV% at even strength.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images The Tampa Bay Lightning announced that defenseman Victor Hedman will not play in Saturday’s game against the Utah Mammoth and will be day-to-day with a lower-body injury. Hedman left Friday’s game against the Colorado Avalanche after he took one shift in the second period and did not return. The team did not provide a reason for his absence during the game, and head coach Jon Cooper didn’t bring Hedman up during his post-game media availability. Hedman skated for only one shift in the second period and did not come out for the final frame. He finished the night with 5:56 of ice time and the Lightning lost 6-3. Through his first nine games, Hedman has two goals and two assists for four points. Now in his 18th NHL season, the 35-year-old native of Ornskoldsvik, Sweden, has 174 goals and 641 assists for 815 points in 1,174 career NHL games. Hedman also has 23 goals and 97 assists for 120 points in 170 career playoff games. He led the Lightning to back-to-back Stanley Cup championships in 2020 and 2021, and helped the team reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2015 and 2022. He won the Norris Trophy for the league’s top defender in 2018 and the Conn Smythe Trophy for Playoff MVP in 2020. The Lightning are 7-3-0 through their first 10 games of 2026-27. Forwards Brandon Hagel and Nikita Kucherov are tied with a team-leading 13 points , while Andrei Vasilevskiy is 5-2-0 with an .884 save percentage .

items.body: New Jersey players excited about ‘huge splash’ of three-time Vezina winner’s acquisition NEWARK, N.J. -- Jack Hughes understands why the trade has created so much noise. The New Jersey Devils center believes the acquisition of Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets deserves every bit of it. "There should be a lot of noise about it," Hughes said. "It's a huge splash for our team, our market. It shows us that our ownership and our management is putting the pieces together to give us a great opportunity to win every night." The Devils acquired Hellebuyck from the Jets on Friday for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to unsigned forward Alexander Command , New Jersey’s second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and its seventh-round selection in the 2027 NHL Draft. The challenge for New Jersey was turning down the volume long enough to play. One day after the trade, they completed an unbeaten homestand (3-0-0) with a 3-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday. That has provided positive momentum before beginning a three-game road trip at the Dallas Stars on Tuesday and welcoming one of the NHL's premier goalies into the group. Hughes already knows what Hellebuyck can bring. The two played together for the United States at the 2026 Winter Olympics and won the gold medal. What stood out to Hughes was the preparation and mentality behind Hellebuyck's performance. "Just extremely dialed in, extremely focused," Hughes said. "A guy that wants to carry the mail, wants to kind of put the team on his back. I'm sure there's going to be a lot of nights where we're going to have to rely on him and on Jake (Allen)." items.body: Register Login Wild Recall Mason Shaw By Brennan McClain | at October 24, 2026 7:00 pm The Minnesota Wild have added familiar depth at forward after losing defenseman Daemon Hunt on waivers. According to a team announcement , the Wild recalled forward Mason Shaw from the AHL’s Iowa Wild. Shaw, 27, is in his second stint with the Wild. Minnesota selected him with the 97th overall pick (fourth round) in the 2017 NHL Draft. He played in the WHL for the Medicine Hat Tigers and made his professional debut in the 2017-18 season. Throughout his first stint with the Wild, Shaw primarily played in the AHL. Still, in the 2022-23 season, Shaw skated in 59 NHL contests, scoring seven goals and 17 points with a -1 rating. Unfortunately, injuries have followed Shaw throughout his career. Before debuting in the NHL, Shaw tore his ACL three times. Towards the end of his first full season with Minnesota, Shaw tore his ACL for a fourth time, putting his career in jeopardy. He dropped off the Wild’s depth chart and later joined the AHL’s Manitoba Moose for two seasons. Although he never returned to the NHL, Shaw’s two years in Manitoba went well. He finished his tenure having scored 32 goals and 81 points in 143 games with a -14 rating. Since returning to the Wild this past summer, Shaw has scored a team-leading three goals and nine points in nine games for Iowa. If he returns to the lineup throughout his call-up, Shaw will play his first NHL contest since April 15, 2024.

items.body: Register Login Jets Recall Elias Salomonsson By Brennan McClain | at October 24, 2026 6:00 pm As expected, the Winnipeg Jets have added a defenseman after Jack St. Ivany was claimed off waivers earlier today. According to a team announcement , the Jets recalled Elias Salomonsson from the AHL’s Manitoba Moose. Salomonsson, 22, has been ramping up in the AHL over the past week. He underwent the knife in April for shoulder surgery, and missed Winnipeg’s training camp and preseason while in recovery. Salomonsson has missed the Jets’ first ten games of the 2026-27 season, and it remains uncertain whether he will be in the lineup for the Heritage Classic tomorrow. Last season, the former second-round pick debuted for Winnipeg. He finished the 2025-26 season with one goal and five points in 32 games with a -6 rating, averaging 17:58 of ice time per game. Although his scoring output left something to be desired, his 51.8% CorsiFor and 91.2% on-ice SV% at even strength show uncommon maturity for a younger defenseman. Fortunately, Salomonsson should have another level to get to offensively. He’s shown it before in the AHL, scoring five goals and 27 points in 53 games throughout the 2024-25 campaign. During his pseudo-preseason over the past week, Salomonsson registered an assist in two games with a -1 rating. While Salomonsson replaced St. Ivany, the Jets will face a similar situation when Josh Morrissey returns from injured reserve due to an upper-body injury. Once Morrissey returns, Salomonsson will likely return to AHL Manitoba since he’s the only defenseman on the roster exempt from waivers.

By Josh Cybulski | at October 24, 2026 5:00 pm The NHL has seen a sellers’ market at the NHL Trade Deadline for at least the past few years, including this past year. The sellers’ market extended well into the draft and summer, as teams paid astronomical prices for top NHL-ready talent. The deadline is still over five months away, and there’s plenty of hockey to be played, but could this season have more sellers than in years past? Only time will tell, but given some teams’ slow starts, the NHL could see more sellers than in some years, which would be good news for buyers. Every year, some teams enter the deadline focused on the future, hoping to move pending unrestricted free agents and other veterans in exchange for future assets. Some teams that might otherwise be sellers instead try to remain competitive, even as their playoff chances fade. This season, with so many teams starting so poorly, it will be interesting to see whether some teams punt on their season earlier than in years past, hoping to beat the sellers’ market and move their assets before the market gets flooded with talent. Perhaps this is the thinking in Pittsburgh, where general manager Kyle Dubas and Penguins management are reportedly looking to move talent to make room for their young prospects. items.title: Ducks’ Leo Carlsson burns Flyers with goal and assist in win
items.summary: Leo Carlsson came within one financial decision of becoming a Philadelphia Flyer last summer. On Saturday, the Anaheim centre found a way to beat the team that tried to pry him away from the Ducks.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Leo Carlsson came within one financial decision of becoming a Philadelphia Flyer last summer. On Saturday, the Anaheim centre found a way to beat the team that tried to pry him away from the Ducks. Carlsson scored and assisted on the game-winner as the Ducks snapped a five-game losing streak with a 5-4 win over Philadelphia. “Attention was on some other guys, so I didn't really feel anything different about it, to be honest,” Carlsson said. “I was never really here, so it wasn't anything different.” The Flyers could use Carlsson's production. After his two-point game, he now leads the Ducks in scoring with 13 points (three goals, 10 assists). His goal was set up by Cutter Gauthier, the player he was referencing, who the fans were paying attention to, as their vitriolic chants still target Gauthier after forcing a trade from the Flyers in January 2024. The Flyers and Ducks have been linked multiple times in the past two years. After acquiring Jamie Drysdale for Gauthier, the Flyers also acquired Trevor Zegras from Anaheim. But the Flyers turned the NHL on it's ear when they tendered the 21-year-old Carlsson to a five-year, $90-million offer sheet on July 3. Its $18 million average annual value was the richest in NHL history at the time. Anaheim matched it six days later, a day before the deadline, keeping Carlsson through the 2030-31 season. Philadelphia kept the four first-round picks it would have owed as compensation. “Did we expect the offer sheet to be this high? No. We did not see that one coming,” Ducks general manager Pat Verbeek said at the time. “But we’re very confident, with the cap going up and the ability of Leo to make strides of improvement and become an elite player, we feel confident this contract will be a good one in the end.” Carlsson

items.title: ‘I hope they know I care about them’: Hellebuyck sends positive message to Jets fans
items.summary: Star goalie Connor Hellebuyck addressed the media in New Jersey the day after he was traded from the Jets to the Devils.
items.body: Mehta had a lot to say about his process, philosophy on the goaltending position, and the work his front office did to facilitate the deal, but Hellebuyck struck a positive tone toward the fan base whose team he had just demanded out of after a 2025-26 season in which they missed the playoffs after claiming the Presidents’ Trophy the year prior. “There’s a lot that I need to say,” Hellebuyck said. “But they have the [Heritage Classic] coming up. So out of respect for them and the celebration of hockey, I’m going to postpone that to a later date. I hope they know I care about them.” Hellebuyck could have his first opportunity to play in front of the fans in Winnipeg when the Devils take on the Jets in Manitoba on November 10, but as Mehta shared during his availability, there has not been a plan put in place for Hellebuyck’s return to play. The 33-year-old has missed the entirety of training camp, the preseason and the regular season as he awaited a trade away from the Jets. The Michigan native leaves Winnipeg as the most decorated player in this iteration of Jets hockey. He captured three Vezina Trophies as the top goalie in the NHL, and in 2025, he became the first goalie to win the Hart Trophy since Carey Price a decade earlier. Hellebuyck backstopped Team USA to its first Olympic gold medal since 1980 last winter in Italy, putting together a performance for the ages in the gold medal game, an overtime win over Canada. Given those accolades, it’s no surprise that Hellebuyck was clearheaded about what’s on his mind now that he’s gotten the trade he wanted. “I’m here to win,” he said. “The only thing I’ve got left on my resume is a Stanley Cup. items.summary: Breaking down the CBA rule that has yielded a discounted salary cap charge for the New Jersey Devils for Connor Hellebuyck this season.
items.body: Register Login Breaking Down Connor Hellebuyck’s Discounted Cap Hit By Brian La Rose | at October 24, 2026 12:30 pm The early assessment of Friday’s Connor Hellebuyck trade has drawn mixed reviews. Some think that the Devils acquired him at a discount while others think the Jets made out rather well. Regardless of your take on the matter, New Jersey did indeed acquire the veteran netminder at a discount. That is, a discount in his cap hit. Section 15.13 (a) of the CBA has a clause that says players who miss time in training camp without permission are subject to a fixed reduction in pay. The clause reads as follows: For each day a Player does not report during Training Camp without his Club’s permission, his pay shall be reduced by 1/275th of his annual Paragraph 1 NHL Salary specified in his SPC without limitation of any other contract rights it may have. Subsection (b) goes on to discuss the requirements for this rule to come into effect. Basically, Hellebuyck had to request an absence, the team had to respond no in writing and allow ample time for Hellebuyck to “cure” and recant his request. All of those things occurred, meaning the above rule was indeed applied. Hellebuyck’s regular cap hit is $8.5MM. Based on the 1/275th per day formula above, the reduced cap charge increases by $30,909.09 per day missed. Winnipeg’s training camp lasted 13 days and he obviously missed all of them. Thus, the reduction is 13 times the daily amount, or $401,818.20. That moves his cap charge from $8.5MM to $8,098,182. That will be Hellebuyck’s cap hit for the rest of the season, before reverting to the $8.5MM number starting in 2027-28 for the rest of his deal. New Jersey acquired the 33-year-old goalie , a three-time Vezina Trophy winner, and Hart Trophy recipient with five seasons remaining on a contract with an $8.5 million average annual value, in a trade with the Winnipeg Jets on Friday. The Devils paid a considerable price -- forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to unsigned draft choice Alexander Command , New Jersey’s second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and its seventh-round selection in the 2027 NHL Draft. It’s a substantial package, but the Devils made the trade without surrendering a first-round pick or one of the foundational players they believe can help them contend with Hellebuyck, Winnipeg's all-time leader among goalies in games played, starts and wins. Connor traded to Devils by Jets in 5-player deal, ending Winnipeg saga He has a 345-208-55 record with a 2.58 goals-against average, .916 save percentage and 45 shutouts in 625 NHL games. That resume alone explains why the move doesn't necessarily contradict Mehta's philosophy as much as it initially appears. "I would say it signals, in my view, even though it's a bigger magnitude trade, it does signal what I think has been our process since I got here, which is everything is about winning," Mehta said Saturday. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s been a start of early struggles for the Philadelphia Flyers since the puck dropped on the 2026-27 NHL regular season, but they’re set to get a little bit healthier as defenseman Rasmus Ristolainen nears his return to the lineup. On Saturday morning, the Flyers activated Ristolainen from injured reserve, making him eligible to return from a nine-game injured absence for Saturday’s home matchup against the Anaheim Ducks . In a corresponding move, the hockey club assigned winger Garrett Wilson to their AHL team, the Lehigh Valley Phantoms. The 31-year-old’s absence stems from a hand injury he sustained three weeks ago, after he started the season with a single goal in his first three games. According to Jordan Hall of NBC Sports Philadelphia, his status for Saturday remains a game-time decision . If the Finnish defenseman can’t lace up on Saturday, his next chance to return to the Flyers’ lineup would come Tuesday, when they take on the Columbus Blue Jackets . However, with the struggles the team has had as the only Eastern Conference team with a worse-than -10 goal differential, any help on the back end would be sorely welcome. Injuries are not new for Ristolainen either, having only reached the 70-game mark once since joining the Flyers in 2021, and appearing unlikely to hit the mark this season, considering the significant absence early in the schedule. The Flyers currently sit second-last in the Metropolitan Division with a 3-6-3 record, ahead of only one team: their upcoming opponent, the Blue Jackets. items.title: Rangers Recall Matthew Robertson
items.summary: The New York Rangers have recalled defenseman Matthew Robertson from AHL Hartford.
items.body: Register Login Rangers Recall Matthew Robertson By Brian La Rose | at October 24, 2026 11:30 am After sending down Justin Dowling , the Rangers didn’t waste much time filling the vacated roster spot. The team announced ( Twitter link ) late Friday that defenseman Matthew Robertson has been recalled from AHL Hartford. With the recall, the team is now back to the maximum of 23 players on the active roster. The 25-year-old was basically a regular with New York last season, playing in 72 games. He chipped in offensively with six goals and a dozen assists in more than 17 minutes per game of playing time. Basically, it looked as if he had secured a spot on their full-time roster. Instead, the team reshaped their back end over the summer, bringing in Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson while fifth overall pick Alberts Smits has been an every-game regular. That pushed Robertson onto the waiver wire early this month, where he somewhat surprisingly passed through unclaimed. Robertson has suited up in six games for the Wolf Pack so far this season and has been fairly quiet offensively, collecting just one assist. He had surpassed the 20-point mark in each of his last three full seasons with them from 2022-23 through 2024-25. It’s unclear if Robertson’s promotion is to play him (perhaps to give Smits a night off) or hedging against injury with Durzi missing the last two practices. Either way, the Rangers need to get Robertson in at least six games with them this season to retain his RFA rights this summer. If they don’t, he’ll be eligible for Group Six unrestricted free agency in July.
